query: Write me a systemd service and timer pair that runs /usr/local/bin/nightly-backup every night at 2:00 local time, and say where each file goes.
result:
Both files go in `/etc/systemd/system/`, and since this is Bluefin, edit them in `~/.dotfiles/bluefin/etc/systemd/system/` first and put them into `/etc` from there. I haven't written or installed anything.

`/etc/systemd/system/nightly-backup.service`:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Nightly backup

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/nightly-backup
NoNewPrivileges=yes
PrivateTmp=yes
ProtectSystem=strict
# Every path the script writes to. Each must exist before the unit starts.
ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/nightly-backup
```

`/etc/systemd/system/nightly-backup.timer`:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Run nightly-backup at 02:00

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 02:00:00
Persistent=true
RandomizedDelaySec=0

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```

`OnCalendar` uses the system's local time zone. `Persistent=true` runs a missed backup at the next boot, for example if the desktop was off at 2:00. `RandomizedDelaySec=0` keeps the start at exactly 2:00. Raise it if you'd rather have jitter.

The `ReadWritePaths=` line is a placeholder. `ProtectSystem=strict` makes the whole filesystem read-only for the service, so the backup fails if the script writes anywhere not listed. If it needs `/var/lib/nightly-backup`, create that directory first, because a missing path stops the unit with a mount-namespacing error. I don't know what the script writes to, so tell me its destination, or I can read the script and fill this in.

To enable it after the files are in place:

```bash
sudo systemd-analyze verify /etc/systemd/system/nightly-backup.{service,timer}
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now nightly-backup.timer
systemctl list-timers nightly-backup.timer
```

Enable the timer, not the service. Your dotfiles gate (`bash scripts/gate.sh`) will need to pass before the dotfiles copy lands.
